neighbours.label: A word for sight or hearing as a working faculty ('visual', 'eyes', 'ears', 'field of vision'), not other body functions
fire: Drivers should keep visual contact with the crew whenever the crane is moving.
The disease slowly damages visual acuity and makes reading small print difficult.
Hunters learn to trust their eyes and ears when they cross open country.
As the sedative wore off, her eyes were open and she followed the nurse.
Older cats may lose visual and auditory function during the final years of life.
The toy must stay inside the baby's field of vision for the game to work.
Bats depend on their ears far more than most other animals in the forest.
New recruits are told to keep their eyes on the road and watch for signals.
quiet: Drivers should keep both hands on the wheel whenever the crane is moving.
The disease slowly damages kidney tissue and makes long walks more difficult.
Hunters learn to trust their legs and lungs when they cross open country.
As the sedative wore off, her fingers were warm and she thanked the nurse.
Older cats may lose muscle and bone mass during the final years of life.
The toy must stay inside the baby's wooden crib for the game to work.
Bats depend on their wings far more than most other animals in the forest.
New recruits are told to keep their boots clean and carry the signals kit.

short: sight or hearing as a faculty
